title: Every face
hook: Jews of every color and background
carry: a whole story, not a question

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ger tzedek, the Jew by choice, and your line: fully Jewish. Today the welcome widens to the whole room.

"And a mixed multitude went up also with them." That's Exodus, on the night the Israelites walked out of Egypt: the text goes out of its way to say others walked out with them. Now step into a synagogue on a Saturday morning. The woman handing out prayer books may trace her family to Baghdad; the man beside you, to Addis Ababa, Kraków, Kochi, or a small town where nobody else was Jewish. A child in the front row was adopted. Someone at the back chose this people as an adult.
screen: `A MIXED MULTITUDE.` → `BAGHDAD, ADDIS ABABA, KRAKÓW, KOCHI.` → `ADOPTED, OR CHOSEN AS AN ADULT.`

segments.voice: The Mishnah asks a strange question. Why did God begin with just one person, one Adam, instead of a crowd? One of its answers: so nobody could ever say to anyone else, my ancestor was greater than yours. Everyone goes back to the same one. Then a picture from the mint: When a king stamps coins from one die, every coin comes out the same. God stamped every human being with the seal of the first person, and not one is like another. In this teaching, sameness is the human way of making things; difference is the divine signature. The prophet Amos goes further. Speaking for God to his own people, he asks: "Are ye not as the children of the Ethiopians unto Me, O children of Israel?" Readers hear it differently. Some hear a warning against pride: being chosen doesn't put you closer to God than a far-off nation. Others hear an embrace reaching all the way to Africa. Either way, the verse sets Israel and a distant people side by side in God's eyes. The faces of the Jewish people tell that story out loud: Beta Israel from Ethiopia, with their own prayers and the festival of Sigd; the Jews of Cochin in India; families from Yemen, Iraq, Morocco and Iran; Ashkenazi families from Europe; Jews by choice, and children of every color growing up in Jewish homes. Some Jews of color have described being asked, again and again, are you really Jewish? Yesterday already answered: someone who belongs, belongs. Each face is a whole story, not a question to be checked at the door.
screen: `WHY GOD BEGAN WITH ONE PERSON.` · `ONE SEAL, AND NO TWO COINS ALIKE.` · `AS THE CHILDREN OF THE ETHIOPIANS.` · `A WHOLE STORY BEHIND EACH FACE.` · then, large: `EVERY FACE.`

segments.voice: Pick a Jewish community you know little about: Ethiopia, India, Yemen, Iran. Hold the questions softly: where did their grandparents walk, what did they carry, what did they sing on the way? You don't need answers; just make room, the way the Mishnah makes room for every face. If you pray, you can give thanks for the people of every look who belong.
Every face. The Mishnah's picture: God stamps every person from one seal, and no two come out alike. Today's word.
Your line: a whole story, not a question. Every face has a road behind it. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish communities and organizations share the histories of Ethiopian, Indian, Mizrahi, Sephardi, Ashkenazi and other Jews through study, festivals, food and personal stories, and some congregations make a point of welcoming Jews of color and Jews by choice.
